name: Crown Hill
title: A hill town climbing in switchbacks to the Crown
axes: x east, z north, y up; metres; the camp at the origin on y 0
description: You start on the Belvedere Shelf, a long park terrace low on the hill, with the Quay and the river wall below you and the whole city climbing away to the north. Every route reads by height: the final court is the top of the hill: 14 m up the Hundred Steps from the gate, then Clock Street and back and forth up the two switchbacks of the Zigzag, so the horde chases you uphill and drops on you from the balustrades above. East runs the open Promenade along the shelf's edge, down a broad flight to the Lower Promenade, then two climbs to a raised hall on Belvedere Heights. South, the Chute drops you down a narrow stair between tenements to the Quay, where a ground-level warehouse door waits at the end of a long open quayside with cranes overhead. West, a ramp sinks into the Hill Cutting, a trench that deepens to 14 m under two footbridges, ending at a sunk tunnel mouth. Rows built against each terrace wall have roofs level with the street above, so the roofs are a second street all over the hill.
